blocks.prompt: 8 Prove that the points whose position vectors are \(A(3\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k})\), \(B(\underline{i} - 2\underline{j} + \underline{k})\), \(C(6\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - 2\underline{k})\), \(D(9\underline{i} + 6\underline{j} - 3\underline{k})\) are coplanar.
blocks.explanation:
A coplanarity proof for four points, like Question 5.
We must show A, B, C, D lie in one plane.
Plan: find \(\overrightarrow{AB}, \overrightarrow{AC}, \overrightarrow{AD}\) and show their triple product is 0.
steps:
Given: the position vectors of \(A, B, C, D\).
To prove: \(A, B, C, D\) are coplanar.
Method: \([\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}] = 0\).

Triple product
\[\begin{vmatrix} -2 & -4 & 2 \\ 3 & 2 & -1 \\ 6 & 4 & -2 \end{vmatrix}\]
\[= -2(-4 + 4) + 4(-6 + 6) + 2(12 - 12)\]
\[= 0 + 0 + 0 = 0\]
Why: All three minors are 0, because row 3 is exactly 2 times row 2.

Conclude and check
\[\overrightarrow{AD} = 2\overrightarrow{AC}\]
\[2(3\underline{i} + 2\underline{j} - \underline{k}) = 6\underline{i} + 4\underline{j} - 2\underline{k} \;\checkmark\]
Why: The triple product is 0, so the four points are coplanar. In fact \(A, C, D\) are on one line, and any line together with a fourth point always lies in a plane.
blocks.final_answer: \([\overrightarrow{AB}\ \overrightarrow{AC}\ \overrightarrow{AD}] = 0\). Hence proved: \(A, B, C, D\) are coplanar.
